title: Quantization technical review - Zenith AI
summary: Deep dive on quantization strategy and expected accuracy/latency tradeoffs for Zenith's LLM workloads. Discussed INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ options, KV-cache impacts, batching strategies, and VPC/on-prem constraints. Agreed to run benchmarks (INT8 vs AWQ vs GPTQ) on Zenith infra and to validate regen cases with targeted eval set.
topics: KV cache and prefix caching behavior
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we're excited to dig into quantization options for your inference workloads - we've got Ravi and Laura from infra/quant teams on the call.
[00:14] Alex Turner: yeah thanks, quick context - we're running a 7B -> 30B ensemble of models for chat and retrieval-augmented prompts; main goals are sub-150ms p50 for 2k tokens and lower cost than FP16 instances, ideally move to dedicated infra in our VPC.
[00:29] Ravi Patel: got it. so first question, what's your current inference stack? are you using Triton / TorchServe / custom?
[00:40] Priya Singh: currently custom k8s with Triton for some endpoints, but mostly our own runner using ONNX conversions. we do prefix caching in front but the kv cache is managed in Redis right now - we want to evaluate moving to local KV cache to lower latency.
[00:58] Laura Gomez: interesting - local KV cached on-GPU is often a big win for repeated multi-turns; we can show numbers. also worth noting that different quant formats interact with kv cache size: e.g. GPTQ's per-tensor packing changes memory layout which can affect cache eviction patterns.
[01:18] Tom Reynolds: wait sorry can you repeat that about GPTQ? i thought GPTQ just q8_0 style, what's per-tensor packing?
[01:27] Ravi Patel: yeah, terminology is messy - GPTQ produces per-channel scales and compressed weight representations. some runtimes (including ours) unpack on the fly into an intermediate layout; that impacts memory bandwidth during KV cache reloads. so you sometimes see higher latency on small-batch single-turns.
[01:44] Alex Turner: ok so concretely, what are tradeoffs between INT8 and AWQ for a 30B model? we care about accuracy on our internal evals as well.
[01:55] Laura Gomez: AWQ generally preserves more accuracy vs naive INT8 for many decoder-only models; INT8 can be fine with calibration and per-channel quantization, but you sometimes get edge-case regressions on arithmetic or long-context completions. FP8 can be a middle ground but needs HW support (A800/FB8) and software stack maturity.
[02:12] Priya Singh: we don't have FP8 on-prem; our infra is 2xA100 and some older V100 fleet. so FP8 is off table for now.
[02:23] Ravi Patel: that matters because FP8 often gives similar latency benefits without as much accuracy loss. for A100-only infra, we focus on INT8 (GPTQ) and AWQ variants. AWQ tends to have slightly higher mem use but better SNR on logits.
[02:40] Alex Turner: how about accuracy regressions - how do you detect and mitigate them? we have a set of 1k prompts used in CI.
[02:50] Maya Chen: perfect - we recommend running an eval suite (we call it 'regress suite') across your prompts and measure rouge/EM/LL delta. typical workflow: run FP16 baseline, then INT8/GPTQ/AWQ variants, compute delta and threshold, then identify offending prompts for manual review.
[03:10] Tom Reynolds: is that automated in your console? or do we run offline?
[03:16] Laura Gomez: we can integrate with Redwood Optimize - we can ingest your prompt set and run batch evals across quant variants; we'll produce per-prompt diffs and a regression alert. we can also export traces to S3 (or your VPC bucket) for you to review.
[03:33] Priya Singh: data residency is required, so S3 in our VPC or gs is fine. encryption with KMS must be supported.
[03:39] Maya Chen: yep - private deployments support bringing your own KMS/HSM and audit logs. we'll share the security docs after the call.
[03:48] Alex Turner: back to latency - you mentioned unpack-on-the-fly for GPTQ causing higher p50 on single-turns. any numbers?
[03:57] Ravi Patel: rough numbers: on our 30B test model, FP16 p50 for 1k context single-turn is ~120ms on 2xA100; GPTQ INT8 often hits 95-110ms for sustained throughput but single-shot can be 130-160ms if unpacking penalties and small batch. AWQ tuned kernels hit ~100-115ms but memory footprint is slightly larger leading to lower max batch. these are ballpark and vary by seq length.
[04:30] Tom Reynolds: what's the impact of KV cache size on throughput? we often have 8-12 turn dialogs and typical prefix length 512 tokens.
[04:40] Laura Gomez: KV cache stored on-GPU reduces network hops and can cut p99 by 30-40% for multi-turn. but if your quantized model increases per-token memory, you might exhaust GPU memory earlier, forcing smaller batch sizes. we recommend hybrid: keep KV on-GPU but use prefix sharing and early eviction heuristics.
[05:02] Priya Singh: we currently shard KV over multiple GPUs; does Redwood support multi-GPU KV sharding?
[05:10] Ravi Patel: yes, our serving runtime supports KV sharding across devices and also cross-device prefix caching; policy config appears in the dedicated config. when you move to dedicated in your VPC, we can tune the shard size and eviction policy.
[05:24] Alex Turner: any gotchas with ONNX pipeline we're using?
[05:28] Laura Gomez: ONNX sometimes loses operator semantics during quant conversion; we often recommend converting from PyTorch to a Redwood-supported format or using hf-llm tooling we provide. also optimizer passes are different for FP16 vs INT8.
[05:40] Alex Turner: got it. ok, let's talk test plan. we need to run fidelity tests and perf bench. what do you recommend?
[05:49] Ravi Patel: recommended plan: 1) run accuracy vs FP16 baseline on your 1k prompt suite for GPTQ, AWQ, INT8; 2) run latency/throughput bench: single-shot p50/p99, sustained throughput at target qps, and multi-turn scenarios with KV on-GPU vs off-GPU. 3) check memory usage and OOMs. 4) if regressions > threshold, run selective mixed-precision or fall back to FP16 for problematic layers.
[06:19] Priya Singh: what's a typical threshold? 1% token-level delta? 2%?
[06:24] Laura Gomez: depends on your metric; for generation quality we usually flag >2% drop in BLEU/ROUGE or >0.2 increase in avg log-loss as a regression needing manual review.
[06:36] Tom Reynolds: on the bench infra, we want to run on our 2xA100. can you run remote benchmarks or do we provide logs?
[06:44] Maya Chen: we can do either. SE team can provide a benchmark harness you run in your environment and upload results, or we can run in a Redwood Dedicated environment with your docker image under VPC peering. both approaches are common.
[06:59] Alex Turner: VL, sorry, VPC peering - is network egress a concern? we have strict egress policies.
[07:05] Ravi Patel: we can do a Private deployment model where control plane is outside but data plane stays inside your VPC; alternatively, bring-your-own infra where we ship our runtime. we'll surface the options in the security doc.
[07:18] Priya Singh: is there a known regression class for instruction-following vs conversational context with AWQ? we've seen hallucinations increase slightly in prior tests.
[07:28] Laura Gomez: yes, some AWQ/GPTQ variants can shift calibration in logits leading to more off-topic completions. We mitigate with temperature scaling, logit biasing, or selective layer fallback. also running an eval on instruction-following prompts helps catch that early.
[07:47] Alex Turner: can you explain selective layer fallback?
[07:50] Ravi Patel: it's where you quantize most layers but keep critical layers in FP16 (usually the first and last few transformer blocks or attention projection matrices). that reduces memory savings but often preserves quality. we can automate a search to find minimal FP16 set that meets your thresholds.
[08:07] Tom Reynolds: what's the overhead to do mixed precision in runtime? is it supported in dedicated?
[08:12] Laura Gomez: supported and common; switching between kernels in runtime can add a few ms when warming up but at steady state it's negligible. memory wise you pay for the FP16 layers' weights.
[08:22] Priya Singh: any examples of when GPTQ failed catastrophically?
[08:26] Ravi Patel: earlier GPTQ tooling didn't handle certain attention layer permutations and caused off-by-one token shifts in decoding for some models; modern toolchains fixed many of those bugs but it's why we run per-prompt regression tests because some prompts trigger the failure modes.
[08:40] Alex Turner: ok. so for our priorities: minimize cost, keep p50<150ms for 2k tokens, and <2% quality drop relative to FP16. are these feasible?
[08:52] Maya Chen: yes, feasible. likely path: try AWQ first on 30B; if memory footprint is too high, try GPTQ with selective mixed-precision fallback. run regress suite and perf bench; if regressions appear, iterate.
[09:05] Ravi Patel: action item for SE: we'll produce a benchmark harness and a tuning doc; for you, provide the 1k prompt set and access to a test node or let us run in dedicated.
[09:16] Priya Singh: we'll prefer to run tests internally and share results - compliance.
[09:20] Laura Gomez: fine, we'll share a dockerized harness and instructions. we'll also include AWQ/GPTQ config presets.
[09:29] Alex Turner: questions from our side: can you support quantized models with function-calling and tool-integration? we rely on function calls for our data access layer.
[09:38] Ravi Patel: yes - function calling is independent of quantization; we handle structured tool outputs in the same stack. latency impact is only from model inference time.
[09:45] Tom Reynolds: one last infra question: if we go dedicated in our VPC, how are upgrades handled? we need maintenance windows.
[09:53] Maya Chen: we allow configurable maintenance windows and can do canary rollouts / A/B to reduce risk. we'll share SLAs in the follow-up.
[10:00] Alex Turner: ok let's recap next steps.
[10:04] Maya Chen: recap: Ravi to deliver benchmark harness and run initial AWQ/GPTQ presets; Zenith to run harness on 2xA100 and upload results; Maya to send security/quantization whitepaper and benchmarks spreadsheet; schedule follow-up review after results - target first week of March.
[10:20] Priya Singh: noted. thanks everyone.
[10:23] Laura Gomez: cool thanks all.
[65:00] [call end], note: timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect (speaker labels and acronyms may be off).
